Source: FEMA_LRS_2024 | Section: Section 6(3) - Liberalised Remittance Scheme
Content: Under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), all resident individuals, including minors, are allowed to freely remit up to USD 2,50,000 (United States Dollars Two Hundred and Fifty Thousand only) per financial year (April - March) for any permissible current or capital account transaction or a combination of both. Any remittances exceeding this threshold of USD 2,50,000 require prior approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Resident individuals are not permitted to make remittances for speculative purposes, margins on foreign exchanges, or illegal operations.

Source: RBI_KYC_DIR_2023 | Section: Para 4.1 - Customer Due Diligence and Re-KYC
Content: Regulated entities must conduct periodic updating of KYC documents (Re-KYC) based on the risk category assigned to the customer. For High-risk customers, full Re-KYC must be executed every 2 years. For Medium-risk customers, Re-KYC must be executed every 8 years. For Low-risk customers, Re-KYC must be executed every 10 years. If a customer fails to submit valid officially valid documents (OVD) within 3 months of the due date, the account operations must be partially frozen, restricting debit transactions.
section: Para 4.1 - Customer Due Diligence and Re-KYC

Source: RBI_UPI_LIMITS_2024 | Section: Para 2.1 - Daily UPI Transaction Thresholds
Content: The standard daily transaction limit for Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transfers is capped at INR 1,00,000 (One Lakh Rupees) per individual per day. However, to facilitate larger payments for specific essential sectors, the limit has been modified. For Capital Markets, Collections, and Insurance payments, the daily transaction limit is elevated to INR 2,00,000. For transactions relating to Educational Institutions and Hospitals, the transaction limit is elevated to INR 5,00,000 per day.

Source: PMLA_MONEY_LAUNDERING_2002 | Section: Section 12 - Reporting Thresholds to FIU-IND
Content: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), every reporting financial institution must maintain a record of all transactions. Reporting entities must report all cash transactions exceeding INR 10,00,000 (Ten Lakh Rupees) or its equivalent in foreign currency, or a series of integrally connected cash transactions that sum to this limit within a calendar month, to the Financial Intelligence Unit - India (FIU-IND) within 7 days of occurrence.

Source: RBI_PPI_WALLET_2023 | Section: Para 3.5 - PPI Balance Loading Constraints
Content: Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs) including mobile wallets are subject to strict loading limits. For semi-closed PPIs (Minimum KYC wallets), the maximum loading balance is capped at INR 10,000 (Ten Thousand Rupees) per month, and total credit in a financial year cannot exceed INR 1,20,000. For full-KYC PPIs, the outstanding balance in the wallet must not exceed INR 2,00,000 (Two Lakh Rupees) at any point in time.

Source: RBI_CREDIT_CARD_2022 | Section: Card Closure Guidelines
Content: If a credit card closure request is not completed by the card-issuer within seven working days, the issuer shall be liable to pay a penalty of INR 500 per day of delay to the customer, provided there is no outstanding balance.

Source: RBI_NEFT_2019 | Section: NEFT 24x7 Operations
Content: The National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) system is available on a 24x7x365 basis. There are 48 half-hourly settlement batches every day. There is no minimum or maximum transfer limit on NEFT transactions.

Source: RBI_DIGITAL_LENDING_2022 | Section: Para 3 - Direct Disbursal to Borrower Account
Content: All loan disbursals and repayments must be executed directly between the bank account of the borrower and the regulated entity without any pass-through or pool account of the Loan Service Provider (LSP).
section: Para 3 - Direct Disbursal to Borrower Account

text:
Source: RBI_CYBER_SEC_2021 | Section: Para 5 - Incident Reporting to CSIRT-Fin
Content: Regulated entities must report all cyber security incidents to RBI and CSIRT-Fin within 2 hours of detection. Root cause analysis (RCA) must be submitted within 7 working days.

Source: RBI_AA_FRAMEWORK_2023 | Section: Para 4 - Account Aggregator Consent Management
Content: Account Aggregators are non-bank financial companies that facilitate consent-based sharing of financial data. AAs cannot store or view customer financial data; data must be encrypted in transit end-to-end.

Source: RBI_CARD_TOKENIZATION_2023 | Section: Para 2 - Device-based Tokenization
Content: No entity in the card transaction chain, other than the card issuer and card network, shall store explicit CoF (Card-on-File) data post September 30, 2022.

Source: SEBI_MF_2024 | Section: Para 1 - Mutual Fund Risk-o-meter
Content: SEBI mandates that all mutual fund schemes must display a Risk-o-meter indicating the risk level (Low to Very High). This must be updated monthly based on portfolio characteristics.

Source: SEBI_AIF_2023 | Section: Para 4 - Alternative Investment Funds
Content: Category III AIFs are permitted to employ leverage up to 2 times their fund size. They must report their leverage limits and risk management framework to SEBI quarterly.

Source: SEBI_IPO_2024 | Section: Para 2 - IPO Lock-in Period
Content: For Initial Public Offerings (IPOs), promoters' contribution of 20% shall be locked in for 18 months from the date of allotment. Non-promoter pre-IPO investors have a lock-in of 6 months.

Source: SEBI_INSIDER_TRADING_2015 | Section: Para 3 - Trading Window Closure
Content: The trading window for designated persons shall be closed from the end of every quarter till 48 hours after the declaration of financial results. During this period, insiders cannot trade in company securities.

Source: SEBI_LODR_2015 | Section: Regulation 30 - Material Events Disclosure
Content: Listed entities must disclose material events to the stock exchanges not later than 24 hours from occurrence. Board meeting outcomes on dividends must be disclosed within 30 minutes of the meeting's conclusion.

Source: SEBI_RIA_2013 | Section: Investment Adviser Fee Caps
Content: Registered Investment Advisers can charge a maximum fee of 2.5% of Assets Under Advice per annum, or a flat fee not exceeding INR 1,25,000 per annum per family across all services.

Source: SEBI_PMS_2020 | Section: Portfolio Management Services Minimum Ticket
Content: The minimum investment amount required for a client to participate in Portfolio Management Services has been increased from INR 25 lakhs to INR 50 lakhs.

Source: SEBI_ESG_2023 | Section: BRSR Core Disclosures
Content: The top 1000 listed entities by market capitalization are required to submit a Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report. The BRSR Core must be reasonably assured by an independent provider for the top 250 listed entities.

Source: SEBI_BUYBACK_2023 | Section: Buyback Tender Offer Process
Content: The timeline for completion of a buyback through the tender offer route has been reduced from T+24 days to T+18 days. The buyback window remains open for exactly 5 working days.

Source: SEBI_REIT_2024 | Section: Minimum Trading Lot
Content: The minimum trading lot for REITs and InvITs has been reduced to 1 unit, enabling retail investors to trade in single units on the stock exchanges.

Source: NPCI_IMPS_2023 | Section: IMPS Transaction Limits
Content: The limit for IMPS transactions has been enhanced from INR 2 lakhs to INR 5 lakhs for channels other than SMS and IVRS. For SMS and IVRS, the per-transaction limit remains INR 5,000.

Source: NPCI_BBPS_2024 | Section: Bharat BillPay Transaction Dispute
Content: Under BBPS, any customer dispute regarding a failed bill payment must be resolved within T+5 days. Failure to do so results in a penalty of INR 100 per day payable to the customer.

Source: NPCI_RUPAY_INTERCHANGE_2023 | Section: Para 3 - Credit Card on UPI Interchange
Content: An interchange fee of 2.0% applies to RuPay credit card transactions on UPI for merchant categories above INR 2,000. Small merchants with turnover under INR 20 lakhs are exempt.
section: Para 3 - Credit Card on UPI Interchange

Source: IRDAI_HEALTH_2024 | Section: Pre-existing Disease Waiting Period
Content: The maximum waiting period for pre-existing diseases in health insurance policies has been reduced from 48 months to 36 months. Insurers cannot reject claims based on PEDs after 36 months of continuous coverage.

Source: IRDAI_BIMA_SUGAM_2024 | Section: Para 1 - One-Stop Insurance Portal
Content: Bima Sugam is a unified digital platform serving as a single window for insurance buying, servicing, and claim settlements across life, health, and general insurance.

Source: PMLA_MONEY_LAUNDERING_2002 | Section: Section 12 - Reporting Thresholds to FIU-IND
Content: Under PMLA, reporting entities must report all cash transactions exceeding INR 10,000,000 (10 Lakhs) or its equivalent in foreign currency to FIU-IND within 7 days of occurrence.

Source: FIU_STR_GUIDELINES_2023 | Section: Suspicious Transaction Reporting
Content: Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) must be filed with FIU-IND within 7 days of arriving at a conclusion that a transaction has no economic rationale or involves proceeds of crime.

Source: IT_ACT_194S_2022 | Section: Section 194S - TDS on Crypto/VDA Transfer
Content: Any person responsible for paying to a resident any sum by way of consideration for transfer of a Virtual Digital Asset (VDA) shall deduct TDS at the rate of 1% of such sum.

Source: IT_ACT_269ST_2017 | Section: Section 269ST - Prohibition of Cash Receipts
Content: No person shall receive an amount of INR 2,00,000 or more in aggregate from a person in a day, or in respect of a single transaction, or in respect of transactions relating to one event, otherwise than by an account payee cheque or electronic bank transfer.
